title: Flank Speed IL5 - Microsoft 365 DoD Tenant (Synthetic)

scope.mission: Notional maritime-support collaboration for 2,400 synthetic workforce accounts organized into six invented mission groups. The scenario covers messaging, meetings, controlled document collaboration, records obligations, and incident coordination. Every account, configuration, event, exception, and assessment observation in this fixture is invented. No actual Navy mission, configuration, tenant, authorization, or assessment is represented.
scope.environment: Flank Speed-inspired Microsoft 365 DoD collaboration tenant, using the Office 365 DoD service environment as public context rather than GCC High. Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, and Teams are candidate in-scope service workloads; their actual tenant provisioning and authorized service boundaries have not been verified. The modeled boundary is tenant configuration and operation plus explicitly qualified candidate inherited service protections.

This is not a complete IL5, FedRAMP High, CNSSI 1253, or tailored DoD baseline. Every target below is notional and requires applicability, inheritance, licensing, and authority review.

assumptions: All numbers, dates, timing objectives, rosters, events, sampling plans, and remediation schedules are synthetic planning inputs as of 2026-09-24.

Microsoft public documentation establishes Office 365 DoD IL5 context and distinguishes it from GCC High; it does not establish authorization or control inheritance for this fixture.

Any Purview, Defender, advanced audit, privileged identity management, sensitivity-label enforcement, conditional-access integration, retention, or eDiscovery function requires cloud-specific availability, SKU, licensing, configuration, and authorized-boundary verification before use. Manual procedural alternatives do not prove equivalent technical protection.
Government-approved identity federation and strong authentication are desired interfaces, not assertions about a deployed CAC/PIV integration or a particular tenant authentication method.
Retention, recycle bins, version history, and legal holds are purpose-limited features, not universal backups or guaranteed recovery of all mailbox, site, OneDrive, or Teams state.

controls.ownership: Shared: tenant identity operator; customer personnel/data owners; candidate provider account-state enforcement.
controls.narrative: The notional operator would create workforce accounts only after the mission owner supplies an approved sponsor, role purpose, and eligibility notice. Monthly reconciliation would compare the invented workforce population with personnel notices, mailbox delegates, Teams memberships, and privileged assignments. Dormant or departed accounts would be restricted through a documented workflow, while records owners separately decide content preservation. Microsoft would supply candidate service-side account-state mechanisms; it would not approve mission eligibility or perform the customer's recertification. External identity authorities retain federation and personnel duties. The included access worksheet illustrates two overdue administrative reviews, not a live directory export. No account management outcome or implementation has been verified.

controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine the full privileged roster and 30 ordinary lifecycle cases against approval and termination records. Interview the identity lead and mission owner about notice handoffs. Test create, modify, disable, and expired-sponsor cases with four nonproduction identities; verify linked workload access without deleting preserved content.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: All 12 privileged assignments have current independent reviews; all 30 sampled ordinary accounts have a valid sponsor and purpose; every tested termination loses tenant access within 4 hours; any exception or unresolved access is a failure. The synthetic worksheet alone cannot satisfy this criterion.

controls.title: Access Enforcement
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant workload and identity operators; customer data owners; candidate provider permission enforcement.
controls.narrative: The notional workload lead would translate data-owner approvals into mailbox delegation, site groups, OneDrive recipients, and Teams membership rather than relying on broad tenant membership. Each administrative change would have a request, approving owner, and verification of the resulting access. Test identities representing an owner, authorized member, unapproved guest, and former member would exercise the same inert content across workload boundaries. Microsoft would provide candidate authorization primitives, while the operator remains responsible for selecting and validating tenant permissions. External recipient eligibility and device protection remain customer duties. Sharing exceptions would never override a missing data-owner decision. The fictional guest-expiry gap prevents a complete access-enforcement assurance claim.
controls.parameters: Notional monthly sample: 10 mailboxes, 10 sites, 10 OneDrive workspaces, and 10 Teams; four identity classes per selected test object; default deny for unapproved guests.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine approved permissions and effective-access exports for the sampled workloads. Interview workload owners about nested groups and link inheritance. Test positive member access and negative guest/former-member access to inert objects, including a Teams-linked SharePoint document.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: Every allowed access matches a documented owner-approved entitlement, and every unapproved or revoked identity is denied. Any unauthorized read, download, delegation, or membership change fails the affected path; policy screenshots alone do not pass.

controls.title: Information Flow Enforcement
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant sharing/mail-flow operators; customer mission/data owners; candidate provider routing and sharing mechanisms.
controls.narrative: The notional operator would maintain an approved flow register connecting each recipient relationship to data purpose, content handling, and expiry. Mail forwarding, site links, individual workspace sharing, and Teams external collaboration would be evaluated as distinct paths rather than one universal switch. Microsoft would supply candidate transport and sharing mechanisms within its documented service scope; optional classification or DLP enforcement would require cloud and SKU verification. The customer data owner retains authority to release information, and recipient systems remain outside this boundary. Invented exercise markings support tests but are not CUI labels. Missing exception expiry would trigger restriction of the affected path until approval and negative-access tests are documented.
controls.parameters: Notional targets: automatic external forwarding denied by default; anonymous links prohibited; guest exception maximum 30 days; test 5 mail rules and 10 links across SharePoint/OneDrive plus 5 external Teams relationships monthly.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine the flow register, rules, link types, and exception ledger. Interview data owners about release authority and prohibited destinations. Test approved and unapproved recipients using inert mail and documents, including an expired link and a prohibited forwarding destination.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: Every sampled external path has current approval and expiry; prohibited destinations, anonymous access, and expired exceptions are denied in every negative test. Any optional enforcement claim must include verified service availability and execution evidence.

controls.title: Least Privilege
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant privileged-access lead; customer approving managers; candidate provider administrative-role primitives.
controls.narrative: The notional identity lead would map each administrative task to the narrowest verified role and a separate administrative identity. Broad roles would require an explicit justification, independent approval, and review of alternate permissions. Routine elevation would be time bounded using a supported mechanism, or an approved manual grant-and-revoke process if optional privileged-management features are unavailable. Microsoft would enforce candidate role primitives but would not determine the customer's mission need. Customer managers retain eligibility and separation-of-duty decisions. Emergency access would require dual custody and immediate review. Two invented assignments lack current review, so this scenario deliberately cannot support a least-privilege conclusion even though the intended workflow is described.
controls.parameters: Notional targets: 12 assignments reviewed monthly; routine elevation no longer than 4 hours where technically supported; 2 emergency identities; emergency-use independent review by next business day.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine all assignments, role justifications, expiry records, and emergency-access custody instructions. Interview assignees and independent reviewers. Test one limited-role administrative action, one prohibited action, one expiry/revocation, and an isolated emergency-access notification path.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: All assignments have current business justification and independent approval; limited identities cannot perform prohibited actions; revoked/elevated access terminates within its approved window; emergency use produces review evidence. Either overdue review is a failure.

controls.title: Remote Access
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant access-policy operator; external customer endpoint/network authorities; candidate provider session interfaces.
controls.narrative: The notional operator would authorize remote access by workforce role, authentication context, and verified posture input rather than treating the internet-facing service as unrestricted. Administrative and ordinary sessions would receive distinct policy scrutiny, with exceptions recorded before access is granted. The tenant boundary includes policy evaluation and access decisions, not customer networks, endpoint software, or remote-access appliances. Microsoft would provide candidate service-side authentication and session mechanisms; exact policy capabilities require DoD cloud and license verification. Customer endpoint and network authorities retain transport-path and device assurance. Unknown or stale posture would be treated as denied until resolved. These are proposed conditions, not evidence of a deployed remote-access architecture.
controls.parameters: Notional targets: strong authentication for every interactive session; posture assertion age at most 24 hours; review all remote-access exceptions monthly; test compliant, noncompliant, unknown, and stale posture states.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine remote-access policy, posture-interface agreements, and exception approvals. Interview identity and external endpoint leads about failure behavior. Test four posture states and an administrative session from an unapproved context in an isolated tenant test environment.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: Approved compliant sessions succeed only with required authentication; noncompliant, unknown, stale, and unapproved administrative contexts are denied. An unsupported policy feature or unverified external dependency leaves the criterion unresolved, not passed.

controls.title: Use of External Systems
controls.ownership: Shared: customer mission/data owner; tenant access/sharing operators; candidate provider external-access controls.
controls.narrative: The notional data owner would approve each external collaboration relationship before the operator enables a guest invitation, external meeting path, or document exchange. Approval would specify recipient eligibility, information purpose, permitted actions, endpoint expectations, and termination conditions. Microsoft would provide candidate restriction mechanisms but would not authorize another organization's system for the customer's mission. External endpoint and recipient-system protections remain separately governed and cannot be inferred from tenant authentication. The operator would test denied access after expiry and record restrictions when recipient assurance is absent. The fictional missing-expiry exception demonstrates an unresolved governance condition, not an actual exposure in Navy or Microsoft systems. No real external connection is established by this fixture.
controls.parameters: Notional population: 20 guest-collaboration exceptions; weekly review of all 20; maximum 30-day exception; unapproved external systems and anonymous access prohibited.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine all exception approvals and the external-system conditions for each relationship. Interview the mission owner and endpoint liaison. Test a permitted recipient, an unapproved recipient, an expired recipient, and an unmanaged-device case against documented policy.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: Every enabled external relationship has an approved purpose, eligible recipient, bounded duration, and applicable external-system conditions; every negative access test is denied. Missing expiry, sponsor, or recipient assurance fails the sampled relationship.

controls.title: Literacy Training and Awareness
controls.ownership: Shared: customer training and mission authorities; tenant operator for service-specific guidance; provider for candidate service notices.
controls.narrative: The notional security manager would provide tenant-specific awareness covering safe sharing, suspicious sign-in reporting, meeting admission, records obligations, and the support-channel boundary. Workforce users would learn that a familiar collaboration interface does not grant authority to release information or upload sensitive content to support. Administrators would receive an additional briefing on separate identities, evidence minimization, and emergency change review. Microsoft may provide service guidance, but customer training completion and comprehension remain customer responsibilities rather than inherited controls. Command training records would be reconciled against tenant access eligibility. Only invented exercise content would appear in training tests. No attendance records, completion rates, or actual user behavior have been supplied.
controls.parameters: Notional targets: initial briefing before access; annual refresher; administrator briefing before role grant; sample 30 workforce training records and all 12 privileged-assignment training records.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine course content and completion-to-access reconciliation for 42 sampled assignment/account records. Interview five users and two administrators. Test comprehension with four synthetic scenarios covering expired links, suspicious access, hold instructions, and support redaction.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: Every sampled access grant has current required training; all interviewed administrators identify emergency/reporting procedures; each participant correctly resolves all four safety-critical scenarios or is retrained before unrestricted access.

controls.title: Event Logging
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant SOC for event selection and reconciliation; provider for supported tenant-visible events; customer for external systems.
controls.narrative: The notional SOC would define required event categories before configuring collection and would reconcile them against actual DoD workload availability. Identity sign-ins, privileged changes, mailbox administration, SharePoint sharing, OneDrive sharing, Teams policy changes, access-policy decisions, and tenant configuration changes form the proposed source set. Microsoft would generate only documented service events; the operator cannot assume access to provider internal telemetry or commercial-cloud audit features. Customer endpoint events remain outside this boundary and require a separate handoff. Each source would have an owner, collection method, expected latency, and evidence of test-event receipt. The invented audit sample omits Teams coverage, so source completeness is explicitly unresolved.
controls.parameters: Notional targets: 8 required source categories; daily presence check; one safe test event per category monthly; ingestion delay target at most 24 hours unless a verified source-specific limit is approved.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine the eight-source matrix and configured collection paths. Interview SOC and workload leads about unsupported event classes. Test one safe representative event for each source, recording event time, receipt time, and retrieval query.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: All 8 sources have verified availability, ownership, and a retrievable test event within the approved delay; absent or unsupported sources remain explicit gaps. Seven of eight sources does not meet the criterion.

controls.title: Content of Audit Records
controls.ownership: Shared: provider for supported source fields; tenant SOC for completeness checks; customer privacy owner for minimization.
controls.narrative: The notional SOC would define a normalized investigation record containing source, event and ingestion times, actor, operation, target, outcome, and correlation information. Normalization would retain original field provenance and distinguish unavailable values from empty strings or invented defaults. Microsoft would determine the supported service-event schema, while the operator would document mapping differences and assess whether each source supports the investigation purpose. Customer privacy owners would approve minimized identifiers and handling rules for exported records. The sample uses aliases and fabricated events only, not real user identifiers. A complete identity event would not establish Teams coverage or field completeness. Missing sources and missing required fields would be reported separately.
controls.parameters: Notional sample: 5 events from each of 8 source categories, 40 total; require 8 investigation fields or an explicitly documented source-specific equivalent; preserve timezone and original event meaning.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine raw-to-normalized mappings and 40 representative records. Interview SOC and privacy coordinators about ambiguous actor/target values. Test reconstruction of who did what to which object and when, including one failed action and one delayed-ingestion event per available source.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: Every sampled record permits unambiguous event reconstruction with approved identifiers and timestamps; no required field is fabricated; all eight sources are represented. Missing source coverage or unexplained field loss fails the affected sample.

controls.title: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant SOC for review and reporting; provider for available telemetry/advisories; customer mission and incident authorities.
controls.narrative: The notional SOC would review administrative grants, suspicious access decisions, sharing-policy changes, and unexpected forwarding in a daily queue. High-priority events would receive expedited triage after ingestion, with the record explicitly separating service collection delay from analyst response time. Microsoft would supply available event data and applicable service advisories; optional Defender or advanced analytics functions require cloud and SKU verification and are not assumed. The customer would decide mission impact and coordinate external endpoint or network investigation. Analysts would document benign explanations, containment requests, and escalation recipients rather than merely marking alerts reviewed. The fabricated audit sample illustrates a queue handoff but does not demonstrate actual detection or analyst performance.
controls.parameters: Notional targets: daily queue review; high-priority triage within 30 minutes of ingestion; weekly trend review; sample 10 dispositions including 3 high-priority administrative/sharing scenarios.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine queue timestamps and ten disposition records. Interview duty analysts and mission incident contacts. Test three inert injected scenarios for a privileged grant, prohibited sharing change, and repeated denied access, including routing when one source is unavailable.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: All three high-priority test scenarios reach an accountable analyst within 30 minutes of ingestion and have documented rationale and escalation; all ten dispositions are traceable. Unavailable source coverage prevents an overall detection-coverage conclusion.

controls.title: Protection of Audit Information
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant SOC/identity operators for access; provider for candidate service protection; external repository owner for exported copies.
controls.narrative: The notional operator would separate audit review from tenant policy administration and limit export and retention changes to approved custodians. Evidence copies would include collection time, source, collector, integrity digest, and custody transfers without embedding secrets or operational content. Microsoft would provide candidate protections for service-held records, but immutable storage or customer-visible tamper guarantees cannot be assumed without current evidence. Any external evidence repository remains outside this boundary and requires its own authorization and access review. Customer privacy and incident authorities would approve disclosure. The included audit text is a synthetic sample, not an integrity-protected production log. Protection would require permission tests and retrieval evidence beyond configuration intentions.
controls.parameters: Notional targets: 2 named audit custodians; quarterly audit-access review; independent approval for retention/export configuration changes; digest and custody entry for every collected evidence batch.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine audit roles, custody records, and export destination approvals. Interview the SOC lead and external repository owner. Test that an ordinary workload administrator cannot alter protected evidence and that an authorized custodian can retrieve and verify a controlled test batch.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: Unauthorized alteration/export attempts are denied, authorized retrieval preserves recorded digests, and every sampled transfer has an accountable custodian and approved destination. Provider or repository protection not evidenced remains unresolved.

controls.title: Audit Record Retention
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant SOC and records officer; provider for supported service retention; external repository owner if separately approved.
controls.narrative: The notional SOC and records officer would agree on audit retention separately from business-content schedules and legal-hold requirements. The proposed searchable and protected-retention periods would be checked against actual service licensing, available exports, and separately approved storage before adoption. Microsoft would document candidate service retention limits; the operator would demonstrate uninterrupted collection and retrieval rather than presume an advanced audit feature exists. Customer records authorities retain schedule and disposition decisions. A hold affecting incident records would suspend conflicting disposal until authorized release. The missing source inventory and fictional hold conflict prevent a complete retention conclusion. Neither one year of audit retention nor content preservation is evidence of general workload backup.
controls.parameters: Notional targets: 90 days searchable audit, 365 days protected retention; monthly retrieval at days 1, 30, and 90 and archive day 365 where such history exists; no disposal during an applicable hold.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine licensed retention limits, export coverage, schedules, and hold instructions. Interview SOC and records owners. Test retrieval across approved age boundaries and a controlled held-record disposition attempt; use historical evidence rather than inventing elapsed retention.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: All required sources are retrievable for the approved periods, applicable holds prevent disposition, and age-boundary evidence is genuine. Insufficient history, missing sources, or conflicting hold rules yields unresolved/fail, not a simulated pass.

controls.title: Control Assessments
controls.ownership: Shared: independent customer assessor and security manager; provider for authorized service evidence; AO separately designated.
controls.narrative: The notional assessment coordinator would prepare an approved plan identifying the forty representative controls, inherited candidates, retained customer duties, sampling populations, and test restrictions. Examine, interview, and test results would be linked to evidence and distinguish design adequacy from operational performance. Microsoft service protections would require an authorized evidence package, not a public compliance page or this narrative. The customer would supply tenant exports, personnel approvals, interface agreements, and independent testers. Samples included here are invented exercises and cannot establish control satisfaction. Six fictional open findings are deliberately retained for workflow testing. An actual assessment would require a complete applicable baseline and independence review before conclusions could support an authorization decision.
controls.parameters: Notional scope: 40 representative controls and 6 open scenario findings; independent review of every proposed finding closure; annual assessment planning plus reassessment after material boundary change.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine the assessment plan, evidence provenance, full baseline mapping, and assessor independence. Interview owner and assessor about inherited duties. Test reproducibility of one selected procedure from each of access, audit, sharing, and recovery using authorized inert artifacts.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: Every assessment conclusion cites valid evidence, actual procedure results, responsible ownership, and applicable scope; all six closures require independent retest. Synthetic samples, missing baseline coverage, or unsigned decisions cannot support a passed authorization gate.

controls.title: Information Exchange
controls.ownership: Shared: customer exchange authorities and mission owners; tenant operator for local restrictions; provider for service interfaces.
controls.narrative: The notional operator would document each external information exchange with a purpose, information category, partner authority, transport assumptions, and conditions for suspension. The flow register includes identity federation, endpoint posture, external recipients, security evidence export, and sanitized support coordination. Microsoft would provide candidate service interfaces, but customer exchange approvals are not inherited from the provider. Recipient systems, external repositories, and support service remain outside the proposed tenant boundary. Customer mission owners would authorize release and require reciprocal responsibilities where appropriate. Internal workload flows would also be recorded to expose permission and records dependencies. The fictional guest exception lacks expiry, and formal exchange approvals are absent, so no connection is represented as authorized.
controls.parameters: Notional register: 10 flows, each reviewed annually and after material change; external exchange approval required before enablement; guest-related approvals expire within 30 days unless renewed.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine all ten flow records and external agreements for purpose, parties, protection, and termination. Interview mission, identity, endpoint, and provider liaisons. Test suspension of one guest exchange and one evidence-export path using inert content and approved nonproduction interfaces.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: Every enabled external exchange has current approval and documented responsibilities; both suspension tests prevent further unauthorized transfer; support data is minimized and separately approved. Missing approval or expiry fails the applicable exchange.

controls.title: Continuous Monitoring
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant security manager and monitoring owners; customer risk authorities; provider for candidate service-change and assurance inputs.
controls.narrative: The notional security manager would maintain a monitoring calendar connecting each activity to a source, threshold, accountable owner, and escalation deadline. Daily audit checks, weekly sharing review, monthly privilege and baseline review, and quarterly restoration exercises would feed a single risk register. Microsoft service advisories and authorized assurance updates would be inputs, not substitutes for tenant monitoring. Customer mission owners would assess impact and retain risk decisions for endpoints, networks, and data use. The operator would record missed activities as gaps instead of reporting a green dashboard from absent evidence. Six open fictional findings remain visible until independent closure review. Monitoring does not make the unsigned decision effective or imply ongoing authorization.
controls.parameters: Notional cadence: daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual activities as listed; monthly owner risk review; missed high-priority activity escalated within 1 business day; all 6 POAMs reviewed weekly.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine the monitoring calendar, thresholds, and six POAM status histories. Interview activity owners and the system owner. Test a missed audit source, expired exception, and overdue milestone to confirm routing and visible unresolved status.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: Every activity has evidence or an explicit missed/unavailable state; each injected threshold breach reaches its owner within the stated deadline; no open finding is automatically marked closed and no monitoring result activates the draft decision.

controls.title: Baseline Configuration
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant change board and workload leads; provider for service defaults and changes; customer mission/privacy authorities.
controls.narrative: The notional change board would maintain a versioned baseline covering tenant identity, administrative roles, messaging, document sharing, Teams policies, audit sources, and records dependencies. Each setting would identify its intended value, available enforcement mechanism, approving owner, and exception condition. Microsoft would document supported service settings and changes, while the customer operator selects and validates tenant values. Provider-managed infrastructure settings are candidate inherited items, not tenant-configurable baseline entries. Customer mission and privacy owners would approve local impacts and external dependencies. The baseline would distinguish unavailable optional features from disabled supported features. The synthetic change worksheet demonstrates format only; no actual export or approved baseline has been supplied.
controls.parameters: Notional baseline: 12 logical components and 24 capabilities; monthly reconciliation; version increment for each approved policy revision; rollback reference and owner required for every changed setting.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine baseline versions, settings exports, and service-availability checks. Interview the change chair and two workload leads. Test comparison of an approved baseline with a controlled changed setting and verify that unsupported product assumptions are flagged.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: Every component has an owned, approved, reproducible baseline; all observed deviations have approved exceptions or tracked corrective actions; no nonexistent/unverified feature is credited as an enforced setting.

controls.title: Configuration Change Control
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant change board and implementers; customer records/data owners; provider for underlying service changes.
controls.narrative: The notional change chair would require a request describing purpose, affected workloads, before-and-after settings, security and privacy impact, testing, and rollback. A reviewer independent of the implementer would authorize tenant policy changes before execution. Microsoft retains its underlying service-change processes; the customer board evaluates communicated effects but does not control provider infrastructure deployments. Customer records and mission owners would approve changes affecting retention, holds, or external sharing. Emergency changes would be time bounded and reviewed the next business day. The invented change sample contains a blocked retention proposal with an unresolved hold conflict. It is not evidence of a production rollout, successful rollback, or approved exception.
controls.parameters: Notional sample: 8 policy changes, including 2 emergency cases; independent approval for 100%; emergency retrospective within 1 business day; no retention change promoted with unresolved hold conflict.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine eight change records and their impact/approval/rollback evidence. Interview the change chair, implementer, and records officer. Test rejection of an unapproved change and a conflicting retention proposal, then rehearse rollback of an inert nonproduction sharing setting.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: All eight changes have independent approval or timely emergency review, verifiable results, and rollback criteria; the hold-conflicting proposal remains blocked. Missing review, untested rollback, or promotion despite conflict fails.

controls.title: Configuration Settings
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant workload and identity operators; provider for supported setting semantics; customer risk owner for exceptions.
controls.narrative: The notional operator would specify restrictive settings for automatic forwarding, anonymous links, guest admission, administrative roles, and access-policy failure behavior. Values would be justified against mission need and verified against the actual DoD service, license, and supported policy interface before enforcement is claimed. Microsoft would define available settings and their semantics; the tenant operator would configure them and test resulting behavior. Customer data owners retain exception decisions and cannot delegate them to a default product setting. Monthly comparisons would identify drift and distinguish planned service changes from unauthorized edits. Optional Purview, Defender, or privileged-management settings would remain conditional. No configuration export has been supplied to demonstrate current values.
controls.parameters: Notional targets: anonymous links disabled; unapproved external forwarding denied; unknown posture denied; configuration drift triaged within 2 business days; 15 security-relevant settings sampled monthly.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine fifteen baseline settings, observed values, and exception approvals. Interview workload and identity leads about policy interactions. Test five denied operations and one intentional nonproduction drift condition, including alert and rollback routing.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: All fifteen observed values match approved settings or current exceptions, all five prohibited operations are denied, and drift is assigned within two business days. Unsupported policy features cannot satisfy an enforcement test.

controls.title: System Component Inventory
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant inventory custodian; provider for service-scope documentation; customer owners for external dependencies.
controls.narrative: The notional inventory custodian would maintain twelve logical service and operational components, each with an owner, two named capabilities, responsibility boundaries, and evidence dependencies. Tenant configuration objects and approved interfaces would be traced to these entries without inventing virtual machines, Azure subscriptions, or physical appliances. Microsoft would maintain its own underlying service inventory and supply relevant boundary evidence; that inventory is not reproduced as customer assets. Customer endpoint, network, federation, and recipient-system owners would maintain separate inventories and identify their interfaces. Monthly reconciliation would compare tenant workload enablement and policy ownership with the scope statement. These entries are synthetic design records only, not discovered or verified deployed components.
controls.parameters: Notional inventory: exactly 12 logical components and 24 named capabilities; every entry has an owner and responsibility split; monthly reconciliation and update within 5 business days of approved scope change.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine all twelve entries, their capabilities, and service/interface scope records. Interview the inventory custodian and external endpoint liaison. Test tracing three enabled workload settings and two external interfaces to correct owners without incorporating external assets into the tenant inventory.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: All twelve entries and twenty-four capabilities reconcile without duplicates or orphaned owners; every sampled setting/interface maps to the correct boundary; no IaaS or endpoint platform is mislabeled as a native tenant component.

controls.title: Contingency Plan
controls.ownership: Shared: customer continuity and mission owners; tenant workload operators; provider for candidate service continuity.
controls.narrative: The notional continuity coordinator would document mission priorities, outage communications, service dependencies, tenant recovery actions, and separately approved alternate collaboration arrangements. The plan would distinguish provider service restoration from customer recovery of content, permissions, ownership, and cross-workload references. Microsoft would supply candidate service continuity commitments and limitations through verified channels, not a blanket promise derived from IL5 documentation. Customer mission owners retain recovery objectives and authorization of external alternatives. Tenant operators would determine whether actual recovery mechanisms can meet those objectives and escalate unsupported cases. The included recovery worksheet is fictional and incomplete. No outage exercise, provider commitment, or mission acceptance has been supplied.
controls.parameters: Notional targets: first mission notice within 30 minutes; priority collaboration recovery within 24 hours; priority content loss no more than 24 hours where verified mechanisms support it; annual plan review.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine the plan, dependency map, provider limitations, and approved alternate arrangements. Interview continuity, workload, and mission owners. Test an outage tabletop with unavailable Teams and linked SharePoint content, recording decision and communication timestamps.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: Every priority function has an owner, supported recovery path, communication route, and approved alternative or explicit unresolved gap; the tabletop reaches mission contacts within 30 minutes. Unsupported 24-hour targets cannot be reported as achieved.

controls.title: Contingency Plan Testing
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant continuity coordinator and independent tester; customer data owners; provider for documented recovery support.
controls.narrative: The notional continuity coordinator would run quarterly isolated exercises covering a mailbox item, site files and permissions, OneDrive departure handoff, and Teams membership with linked content. Each exercise would record prerequisites, expected results, actual timing, unsupported objects, and data-owner reconciliation. Microsoft would provide documented service mechanisms and support limits, while the customer executes and evaluates tenant recovery actions. External identity and network continuity would be coordinated with their separate owners. Retention or version history would be used only where verified to support the specific test, never as a universal backup claim. The supplied worksheet invents one mailbox result and leaves other cases incomplete; it is not a real exercise report.
controls.parameters: Notional cadence: quarterly; 4 workload classes; at least 3 inert objects per workload; independent observer and data-owner reconciliation required; improvement plan within 10 business days.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine exercise plans, source-object manifests, timings, and reconciliation records. Interview continuity and workload leads. Test all four workload classes in an authorized isolated environment, including one intentionally unsupported recovery case and communication fallback.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: All twelve minimum test objects are reconciled for content and required metadata/permissions, all four workload classes are exercised, timing is measured, and unsupported cases have approved treatment. The fictional partial worksheet does not pass.

controls.title: System Backup
controls.ownership: Shared: customer continuity/data owners for recoverability needs; tenant operators for supported recovery sources; provider for documented service mechanisms.
controls.narrative: The notional operator would identify which workload objects require recoverable copies, which service mechanisms actually preserve them, and which gaps need a separately authorized solution. Configuration exports, content recovery sources, permissions, and ownership metadata would be evaluated separately. Microsoft would describe candidate service preservation and recovery behavior; customer expectations cannot be inferred from retention, recycle bins, version history, or legal holds alone. Customer mission and records owners retain recovery requirements and disposition authority. Third-party backup is outside this fixture and cannot silently fill a gap. The recovery-source register would record protection, age, access, and testability. No actual backup inventory or comprehensive restore evidence is supplied.
controls.parameters: Notional target: recoverable priority content age at most 24 hours where supported; weekly tenant-configuration export review; monthly recovery-source inventory; 3 content objects plus permission/ownership metadata checked per workload.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine workload recovery-source inventories, age/protection evidence, and retention/hold dependencies. Interview mission and continuity owners. Test retrieval of three objects and required permissions/ownership metadata for each workload from a verified recoverable source.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: Every priority object class has an evidenced protected recovery source meeting the approved age target and a successful reconciled retrieval; missing permissions, unsupported object types, or reliance solely on retention claims leaves the requirement unmet.

controls.title: System Recovery and Reconstitution
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant continuity/workload operators; customer mission/data owners; provider for underlying service restoration.
controls.narrative: The notional operator would reconstitute tenant collaboration only after verifying content integrity, permissions, ownership, audit visibility, and linked-workload references. A provider service-health recovery notice would be an input, not sufficient proof that customer mission state is restored. Microsoft would restore underlying service functions under its verified arrangements; tenant operators would perform available customer recovery actions and document unrecoverable states. Customer data owners would reconcile restored objects and approve resumption of mission use. External endpoint and identity dependencies would remain separately validated. The invented worksheet does not establish recovery timing or integrity for all workloads. Any unmet objective would remain a tracked gap rather than an assumed successful restoration.
controls.parameters: Notional targets: priority collaboration reconstitution within 24 hours where supported; verify 3 objects per workload plus permissions and ownership; mission-owner signoff required before closing an actual recovery incident.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine recovery runbooks, before/after manifests, and acceptance records. Interview continuity and mission owners. Test restore and reconstitution for mailbox, site, OneDrive, and Teams-linked artifacts, including revoked-user denial and audit generation after recovery.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: All required objects, permissions, owners, and links reconcile; revoked users remain denied; audit events remain available; measured recovery meets the approved objective or an explicit risk decision is documented. No fictional sample can establish completion.

controls.title: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
controls.ownership: Shared: tenant identity operator; external customer identity issuer; provider for supported authentication mechanisms.
controls.narrative: The notional identity lead would require a unique workforce identity and approved strong authentication for each interactive organizational user. Administrative access would use a separate identity with an explicitly approved authentication path and role grant. Microsoft would supply candidate service-side identity validation mechanisms, but the exact government federation and authentication integration must be verified rather than assumed. External customer authorities retain identity proofing, credential issuance, eligibility, and revocation responsibilities. The operator would test rejected credentials and revoked identities without recording secrets. Shared user accounts would not substitute for individual accountability. The access sample highlights missing administrative review evidence; neither that worksheet nor public service documentation establishes authentication deployment or effectiveness.
controls.parameters: Notional targets: unique identities for all 2,400 workforce accounts; strong authentication on all interactive sessions; test 10 ordinary and all 12 privileged assignments; no shared interactive workforce identities.
controls.assessmentProcedure: Examine identity uniqueness, authentication policy, federation trust, and administrative assignment approvals. Interview identity issuer liaison and tenant lead. Test valid, missing-factor, revoked, and mismatched-identity sign-ins with nonproduction identities and no credential disclosure.
controls.acceptanceCriterion: Every sampled identity is uniquely attributable and approved; all invalid/revoked or insufficient-authentication tests are denied; separate privileged identity and current approval are evidenced. Missing review or unsupported authentication assumptions remain unresolved.

controls.title: Authenticator Management
controls.ownership: Shared: customer authenticator issuer and custodians; tenant identity operator; provider for supported revocation/session behavior.
controls.narrative: The notional operator would document the lifecycle of approved authenticators, including enrollment authorization, compromise reporting, replacement, revocation, and emergency access custody. The fixture intentionally contains no passwords, private keys, recovery codes, or real certificate identifiers. Microsoft would provide candidate service handling for supported authentication methods and session invalidation, while external customer issuers retain credential proofing and issuance duties. Tenant administrators would coordinate revocation and test residual access rather than assume issuer revocation instantly terminates every session. findings.title: Synthetic gap: two privileged assignments lack current independent review
findings.observation: In the invented worksheet as of 2026-09-24, two of twelve privileged assignments lack current independent review: exercise-admin-11 last reviewed 2026-07-31 and exercise-admin-12 last reviewed 2026-08-15. Ten other entries are fictional current-review examples, not accepted approvals. The authoritative roster is not supplied. This is a scenario finding only, not an observation about a Navy tenant or Microsoft service.
findings.impact: If the condition existed operationally, unjustified administrative privileges could persist and weaken accountability for tenant-wide policy changes. The fixture demonstrates review and closure workflow risk, not actual compromise.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile all twelve assignments to authoritative eligibility and task need; independently approve or remove each; verify effective denial after removal; establish monthly review with escalation for overdue items and separately verify any optional privileged-management tooling.

findings.title: Synthetic gap: guest-sharing exception lacks expiry and complete exchange approval
findings.observation: One of twenty invented exception records, the exercise-site-blue proposal in the change worksheet, has no expiry and only a draft approval field. No live link was created and the complete recipient/exchange register is not supplied. The scenario extends review to OneDrive and Teams because those paths share the intended exception governance, not because actual cross-workload exposure was observed.
findings.impact: An operational equivalent could allow external collaboration beyond the sponsor's intended period or without compatible processing authority. The magnitude of any real exposure is unknown and no disclosure is asserted.
findings.recommendation: Keep the proposed exchange restricted; obtain mission/privacy and recipient-system approval, set at most thirty-day expiry, inventory related links/memberships, and demonstrate revocation with negative-access tests for all affected workload paths.

findings.title: Synthetic gap: Teams policy events absent from audit-source coverage
findings.observation: The invented audit worksheet represents seven of eight required source categories and omits Teams policy events. No real collection run, event availability verification, schema mapping, or retention retrieval was performed. The missing source is a fictional evidence/coverage condition, not a claim that Microsoft does not supply such events.
findings.impact: An operational blind spot could prevent timely review of collaboration policy changes and leave investigation or retention requirements unmet. Coverage and timeliness cannot be demonstrated from the sample.
findings.recommendation: Verify DoD service/SKU event availability, map supported Teams events, configure only approved collection paths, collect safe test events, validate required fields and ingestion timing, and document residual gaps if the required events are unavailable.

findings.title: Synthetic gap: recovery rehearsal does not cover all workloads or permissions
findings.observation: The fictional recovery worksheet scripts one mailbox item and a partial SharePoint comparison, leaves permissions pending, and does not rehearse OneDrive or Teams. It does not satisfy the planned twelve-object/four-workload scope. There are no actual restore logs, supported recovery-source inventory, or data-owner reconciliation records.
findings.impact: If an operational plan relied on this level of coverage, mission recovery timing, content completeness, permissions, and ownership could remain uncertain. No provider outage, data loss, or service defect is alleged.
findings.recommendation: Verify recoverable object types and source limits first; execute an authorized isolated four-workload rehearsal with at least three inert objects each; reconcile permissions/ownership/links and measure timing; address unsupported recovery cases through explicit risk decisions.

findings.title: Synthetic gap: provider inheritance and cryptographic applicability evidence not supplied
findings.observation: The fixture contains public-context references but no current authorized provider package, tenant-applicable service boundary, responsibility matrix, cryptographic mechanism/module applicability, or provider assessment evidence. The gap is absence of evidence in this synthetic package, not a finding that Microsoft lacks controls or that a real Navy authorization is invalid.
findings.impact: Crediting inherited physical, maintenance, platform, boundary, or cryptographic controls without applicable evidence could materially misstate an authorization basis. Public service inclusion alone cannot resolve the uncertainty.
findings.recommendation: Request the appropriate authorized provider/customer-responsibility evidence through approved channels; reconcile exact DoD services and cryptographic requirements; document retained duties and unsupported claims; obtain independent applicability review before any inheritance credit or real decision.

findings.title: Synthetic gap: blocked retention proposal lacks resolved legal-hold precedence
findings.observation: The invented exercise-site-green change proposes a two-year disposition rule while a preservation instruction is also listed; the conflict review is missing. The proposal is explicitly blocked and no policy promotion or deletion occurred, supporting the Low scenario rating. Actual records authority, hold scope, and service feature behavior are not supplied.
findings.impact: Unresolved instructions could cause future misconfiguration or unauthorized disposition if a blocked proposal were promoted. This is not a claim of existing legal-hold failure or data destruction.
findings.recommendation: Keep the proposal blocked; obtain records/counsel authority, reconcile retention versus preservation across affected workloads, verify supported feature behavior, test held and eligible objects, and require independent approval before promotion.

procedures.title: Notional identity onboarding, privilege review, and departure handoff
steps: Receive an authoritative customer eligibility or departure notice through an approved channel; record receipt time and mission owner without copying unnecessary personnel details.
For onboarding, verify sponsor, purpose, training, unique identity, and approved authentication interface before proposing any tenant access.

For administrative access, select the narrowest supported role, use a separate identity, obtain independent approval, and set an approved duration; verify cloud/SKU availability before relying on optional elevation tooling.
For departure, initiate tenant restriction and role removal within the notional four-hour window, coordinate issuer revocation externally, and test workload and residual-session access.
Send mailbox/OneDrive preservation and successor decisions to records and mission owners; do not equate disablement with permission to delete content.
Reconcile all twelve privileged assignments monthly and thirty ordinary accounts; document current decisions and overdue reviews separately.
Preserve minimized access evidence, route the two fictional overdue reviews to FS-POAM-001, and request independent retest before proposing closure.
procedures.exitCriteria: An actual case would require authoritative approval/notice, attributable actions, denied unauthorized access, preservation/ownership handoffs, and independent review. This fixture supplies only an invented worksheet and cannot meet operational exit criteria.
procedures.limitations: No real account operations, authenticator material, personnel records, or approved federation configuration is included. External issuance and endpoint/network duties remain outside the tenant boundary.

procedures.title: Notional tenant policy change and drift control
steps: Record the proposed setting, baseline version, affected components/workloads, reason, implementer, and independent reviewer.
Verify that the setting exists and is supported in the intended DoD cloud/SKU; identify provider-controlled behavior rather than inventing a tenant setting.
Review security, privacy, sharing, audit, records/hold, and recovery impacts with the relevant owners; keep unresolved conflicts blocked.
Define inert test cases, expected allowed/denied behavior, rollback conditions, and evidence to collect without secrets or operational content.
Obtain independent approval before any authorized test or rollout; emergency actions require documented authority and next-business-day retrospective.
Compare observed before/after values and execution results; rollback only through approved authority when exit criteria fail.
Update the baseline and inventory only after verified outcomes; retain drift as an unresolved issue rather than changing expected values to hide it.
procedures.exitCriteria: Actual change completion would require approval, verified supported settings, passing positive/negative tests, rollback readiness, and updated evidence. The retention proposal in FS-EV-003 remains blocked and FS-FIND-006 remains open.
procedures.limitations: The sample is a proposal worksheet, not an executed change. The tenant board cannot authorize provider infrastructure maintenance or assume optional product availability.

procedures.title: Notional external sharing and exception lifecycle
steps: Receive a mission-purpose request identifying recipient organization, information category, intended workload paths, duration, and accountable sponsor.
Obtain recipient eligibility, external-system conditions, privacy/release authority, and data-owner approval before enabling any exchange.
Verify actual sharing/federation feature support; default-deny anonymous and unapproved external access rather than assuming labels or DLP provide enforcement.
Set a named-recipient restriction and expiry no longer than thirty days where supported; use documented approved controls and identify unsupported expiry mechanisms as gaps.
Test an approved recipient and unapproved/expired recipient with inert content across each affected site, OneDrive workspace, or Teams relationship.
Review all twenty notional exceptions weekly, contact sponsors seven days before expiry, and revoke unrenewed or withdrawn approvals.
Verify denied access after revocation, retain the evidence and approval trail, and submit prospective FS-POAM-002 closure material for independent review.
procedures.exitCriteria: An actual exchange requires complete purpose/recipient/authority/expiry records and verified enforcement, including denied expired access. The invented missing-expiry proposal is not eligible for enablement or closure.
procedures.limitations: No external invitation or content transfer is performed. Recipient endpoints and systems remain outside scope; optional Purview/label/DLP behavior requires cloud/SKU and coverage verification.

procedures.title: Notional incident triage, evidence preservation, and reporting
steps: Record event time, ingestion time, source, actor/target aliases, suspected impact, and confidence; distinguish a source gap from an actual security incident.
Triage high-priority events within thirty minutes of ingestion and identify the authorized containment decision maker.
Preserve available records with provenance, collection time, integrity digest, and custody; restrict access and avoid collecting content unrelated to the investigation.
Coordinate tenant identity restriction, role removal, or sharing revocation using approved authority; hand external endpoint/network investigation to its separate owner.
Notify the internal incident authority within the notional one-hour exercise target and apply actual customer-mandated deadlines only after they are established.
If provider escalation is needed, draft only minimized sanitized workload/timing details and obtain handling approval; support remains outside the service accreditation boundary.
Reconcile recovery with mission/data owners, retain lessons learned and unresolved gaps, and obtain independent review before closing any actual incident.
procedures.exitCriteria: Actual handling requires attributable decisions, preserved evidence, authorized reporting, verified containment/recovery, and mission acceptance. No incident or reporting action occurred in this fixture.
procedures.limitations: Example.test contacts are nonoperational. No real reporting authority or regulatory deadline is asserted. Optional Defender, advanced audit, or external SIEM integrations are not assumed.

procedures.title: Notional continuity and four-workload recovery rehearsal
steps: Confirm mission priorities, approved recovery objectives, external dependencies, and authorized isolated test scope with the system and data owners.
Inventory actual recoverable sources and service limits for mailbox items, SharePoint content/permissions, OneDrive ownership, and Teams membership/linked content.
Select at least three inert objects per workload and record content, owner, permissions, references, recoverable age, and expected outcomes before any test.
Verify that chosen mechanisms and prerequisites are available in the DoD cloud/SKU; document unsupported objects instead of treating retention/version history as universal backup.
Execute only authorized isolated recovery actions, measure real elapsed time, and record errors and dependencies without deleting production content.
Compare content, ownership, permissions, links, revoked-user denial, and audit visibility with the pre-state; obtain independent observation and data-owner reconciliation.
Record objective deviations and unsupported recovery paths in the continuity plan and FS-POAM-004; request explicit risk treatment and independent retest before closure.
procedures.exitCriteria: An actual exercise needs all four workload classes and at least twelve objects reconciled, measured timing, supported recovery-source evidence, and independently reviewed limitations. The partial invented worksheet does not meet this threshold.
procedures.limitations: No restore commands were executed. Provider service restoration is not customer content restoration. Third-party backup and external continuity platforms are excluded and cannot silently satisfy gaps.

procedures.title: Notional records hold, disposition, and conflict resolution

Block proposed disposition and policy promotion when preservation scope, release authority, or conflicting instructions are unresolved.
Test at least five held and five eligible inert objects in an authorized isolated scope, recording preservation and documented deletion lifecycle.
Require records/counsel release and independent change approval before any affected disposition; distinguish logical deletion from physical media sanitization.
Retain release, test, and conflict-resolution evidence for independent FS-POAM-006 review; report unavailable historical retention evidence honestly.
procedures.exitCriteria: An actual disposition requires valid authority, resolved conflicts, verified workload behavior, release where applicable, and independent approval. The invented blocked proposal remains unresolved and no content is disposed.
procedures.limitations: No legal instruction, approved government retention schedule, media certificate, or real hold exists here. Preservation and retention do not guarantee backup or complete restore.

procedures.title: Notional assessment evidence custody and inheritance review
steps: Classify each requested item as an original authorized source, a derived copy with provenance, a synthetic sample, or not supplied; never promote a sample into operational evidence.
Record owner, applicable service/component/control scope, collection date, review cycle, handling restrictions, and integrity/custody details for actual received evidence.
Request provider packages only through legitimate approved channels; confirm exact DoD service applicability and distinguish GCC High and excluded support service.
Map candidate inherited duties separately from tenant configuration and retained customer endpoint, network, personnel, privacy, and mission duties.
Execute authorized examine/interview/test procedures against the complete applicable baseline, retaining negative results and evidence limitations rather than selecting only passing examples.
For each proposed POAM closure, require actual corrective-action evidence and independent retest; leave closureEvidence empty until material is genuinely submitted.
Present residual risk and unresolved evidence to a real designated decision authority; no fixture status, import action, or planned date activates an authorization.
